summary: Round r1 (restricted network): research design and source leads only; no empirical values recorded. Q1 (which economies sustained high growth for 25+ years and from what starting income) will be answered by applying three spell definitions (Growth Report 2008; Hausmann-Pritchett-Rodrik 2005 accelerations; Berg-Ostry-Zettelmeyer 2012 / Kar et al. 2013 structural breaks) to Maddison Project Database 2023 (doi:10.34894/INZBF2) and Penn World Table 11.0 (doi:10.34894/FABVLR), with WDI for investment, saving and export shares. Q2 (preconditions) is framed from the growth-spell literature: openness and export orientation, macro stability, high saving and investment, credible policy continuity, equality, demographic transition. Q3 (transferability) is assessed qualitatively: sea access is structurally absent in Nepal and the East Asian coastal manufacturing-export model does not transfer directly; landlocked precedents (Botswana, Bhutan, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Laos) relied on mineral rents, hydropower exports to a neighbour or public-investment-led strategies; premature deindustrialisation and remittance-driven real appreciation under the INR peg further weaken the manufacturing route; institutions and savings transfer partly; energy and demographics differ in kind. All quantitative items are pending retrieval; regression-to-the-mean evidence (Pritchett-Summers 2014) must be used to bound long-horizon trajectories in 01C.

findings.claim: Q1: Identification of economies that sustained high real per-capita (and total) GDP growth for 25+ years, with spell start/end dates and starting income level
findings.note: Requires MPD 2023 country-year GDP per capita and population (doi:10.34894/INZBF2) and PWT 11.0 rgdpna/pop (doi:10.34894/FABVLR). Apply (a) the Growth Report 25-year high-growth definition, (b) Hausmann-Pritchett-Rodrik acceleration filter, (c) Berg-Ostry-Zettelmeyer / Kar-Pritchett-Raihan-Sen structural-break dating. Report starting income in both MPD 2011 int$ and PWT 2021 PPP$ with vintage labels.

findings.claim: Q1: The Growth Report (2008) list of sustained high-growth economies and its exact threshold definition
findings.note: Retrieve The Growth Report PDF (openknowledge.worldbank.org handle 10986/6507) and transcribe the list and the growth threshold from the report text. Secondary summaries (not retrieved evidence) name Botswana, Brazil, China, Hong Kong SAR, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Malta, Oman, Singapore, Taiwan Province of China and Thailand; treat as a provisional screening list only until verified.

findings.claim: Q1: Growth-spell duration statistics (distribution of spell lengths, survival probabilities by duration, hazard of spell ending by income level)
findings.note: Compute from MPD 2023/PWT 11.0 using the three identification methods; compare with published duration results in Berg-Ostry-Zettelmeyer (2012), Eichengreen-Park-Shin (2012) and persistence results in Pritchett-Summers (2014 NBER w20573).

findings.claim: Q2: Investment (gross capital formation) and saving rates during and at the start of each sustained spell
findings.note: WDI NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS, NY.GNS.ICTR.ZS, NY.GDS.TOTL.ZS (from 1960 where available) and PWT 11.0 csh_i. Note that PWT csh_i is at current PPPs and differs conceptually from WDI national-price shares; keep both.

findings.claim: Q2: Export shares and export composition (manufactures share) during sustained spells
findings.note: WDI NE.EXP.GNFS.ZS, TX.VAL.MANF.ZS.UN; PWT 11.0 csh_x. Record separately for landlocked vs coastal comparators.

findings.claim: Q2: Initial-condition benchmarks (institutions, education, demographics, energy access) at spell start for comparators
findings.note: PWT hc (human capital index), WDI SP.POP.DPND and SP.POP.1564.TO.ZS, EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC / EG.ELC.ACCS.ZS; institutional indicators follow Johnson-Ostry-Subramanian (2010) benchmarking method. WGI only begins in 1996, so earlier spell starts require alternative historical institutional measures (e.g. Polity/V-Dem) — flag as data gap.

findings.claim: Q2 (qualitative, lead-based): the literature identifies openness/export orientation, macroeconomic stability, high saving and investment, market allocation and a committed capable state (Growth Report 2008); income equality, democratic institutions, manufactured-export orientation and avoidance of overvaluation for spell duration (Berg-Ostry-Zettelmeyer 2012); trade expansion at accelerations (Jones-Olken 2008); demographic transition (Bloom-Williamson 1998); and factor accumulation as the dominant proximate source in East Asia (Young 1995) as recurring accompaniments of sustained growth
findings.note: Characterisation of paper conclusions taken from abstracts/search results, not yet retrieved; to be confirmed against full texts in r2 and upgraded to cited observations. No magnitudes are asserted.

findings.claim: Q3: Nepal's current values for each precondition (investment, saving, export share, manufacturing share, remittances, dependency ratio, electricity use, human capital) against comparator values at spell start
findings.note: Needs WDI/PWT series for NPL plus Nepal official series (NSO national accounts, NRB BoP) on a fiscal-year basis (mid-July). WDI Nepal series are labelled by calendar year but are compiled from fiscal-year national accounts — document the conversion before comparing.

findings.claim: Q3 (qualitative): sea access is structurally absent for Nepal, as for Botswana, Bhutan, Laos, Rwanda and Ethiopia among candidate comparators, whereas nearly all East Asian sustained growers had direct sea access; the landlocked literature (Faye et al. 2004; Limao-Venables 2001; Gallup-Sachs-Mellinger 1999; Paudel 2014) indicates the penalty operates through transit-neighbour dependence and trade costs, and that governance, openness and coordinated transit infrastructure moderate it
findings.note: Geographic status is definitional; channel characterisation is from paper abstracts pending full-text retrieval. Size of the penalty is pending (no magnitude asserted).

findings.claim: Q3: Magnitude of the landlocked growth/trade penalty applicable to Nepal
findings.note: Retrieve Limao-Venables (2001), Paudel (2014, 2018), UN-OHRLLS 'Development Economics of Landlockedness'; extract coefficient estimates with specification, sample and period. Complement with World Bank LPI and trade-cost data (Agent 07/22 domain).

assumptions.text: A 'sustained high-growth spell' is analysed under three alternative definitions (Growth Report 25-year threshold; HPR acceleration filter; structural-break dating) and results are reported for each; no single definition is privileged.

Comparator set is stratified: (i) Growth Report sustained growers; (ii) landlocked sustained or near-sustained growers (Botswana, Bhutan, Laos, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Uganda, with Burkina Faso and landlocked Central Asian economies as sensitivity cases); (iii) South Asian neighbours (India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka) and Nepal's own history; (iv) remittance-dependent economies (e.g. Philippines, Tajikistan, Kyrgyz Republic). Final membership is determined by the Q1 computation, not by this list.

Growth is measured as real GDP per capita at constant prices (MPD cgdppc/rgdpnapc, PWT rgdpna/pop, WDI NY.GDP.PCAP.KD). Nominal USD and exchange-rate effects are excluded from spell identification and handled separately by 01A/01C for the US$3T arithmetic.

Transferability is judged per precondition on three dimensions: (a) is it present in Nepal, (b) is it policy-addressable within a 25-45 year horizon, (c) is there any landlocked precedent where it was achieved or substituted. These are qualitative judgements until r2 data are retrieved.
Historical base rates for spell persistence are descriptive, not probabilities for Nepal; consistent with CLAUDE.md, no probability of attaining any trajectory is assigned.

challenges.text: Growth accounting for Nepal should be run on the same PWT 11.0 vintage (and ICP 2021 PPP base) used for comparators so that TFP and capital-deepening comparisons are like-for-like; fiscal-to-calendar-year conversion must be documented.

Required-growth trajectories for 2050/2060/2070 should be compared against the empirical distribution of spell durations and the regression-to-the-mean evidence (Pritchett-Summers 2014) before being presented; trajectories exceeding any historical precedent in duration should be flagged as without precedent.

Landlocked transit-cost and logistics data (LPI, transit times via Kolkata/Visakhapatnam and prospective China routes) are needed to quantify the sea-access precondition; please supply the corresponding observations when available.

The energy precondition for Nepal differs from East Asian comparators (hydropower endowment, seasonal deficit, export dependence on India's grid); comparison with Bhutan's hydropower-led model requires Nepal electricity-balance and export data.

uncertainty: High. No data have been retrieved in r1, so the comparator set, spell statistics and precondition benchmarks are all pending. Spell identification is known to be sensitive to the definition used, to PPP vintage (ICP 2011/2017/2021 bases in MPD vs PWT) and to data revisions, so results will be reported under multiple definitions and vintages. Transferability judgements are qualitative and based on paper abstracts pending full-text reading; the small number of landlocked, non-resource sustained growers makes inference about Nepal from precedent inherently weak. Historical base rates are descriptive and are not probabilities for Nepal.

comparator_set.method: Screen all MPD 2023 / PWT 11.0 economies with the three spell definitions (01B-A1); stratify per 01B-A2; record for each: spell start/end years, starting real GDP per capita (MPD 2011 int$ and PWT 2021 PPP$), landlocked flag, population size class, resource-export dependence, remittance dependence.

data_required: MPD 2023 GDP per capita and population, all countries, 1950-2022
PWT 11.0 rgdpna, pop, csh_i, csh_x, hc, rnna, rtfpna, 1950-2023
WDI NY.GDP.PCAP.KD, NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS, NY.GNS.ICTR.ZS, NE.EXP.GNFS.ZS, TX.VAL.MANF.ZS.UN, BX.TRF.PWKR.DT.GD.ZS, SP.POP.DPND, EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC, 1960-latest
growth_spell_statistics.method: For each definition: count of spells, distribution of durations, Kaplan-Meier survival of spells by duration, spell-end hazard by income level (cf. Eichengreen-Park-Shin), mean/median investment and export shares within spells, and share of spells occurring in landlocked economies. Sensitivity: PWT 11.0 vs 10.01 vintage and MPD vs PWT, keeping both where they disagree (find_conflicts).

transferability_assessment.status: pending (qualitative framework complete; quantitative benchmarks pending)

sea_access.nepal_status: structurally absent (landlocked between India and China); cannot be changed by policy, only mitigated via transit agreements, multimodal corridors, dry ports and trade facilitation
sea_access.transfers: No. East Asian coastal export-platform model does not transfer directly. Relevant precedents are landlocked: Botswana (mineral rents, not manufactured exports), Bhutan (hydropower exports to a single neighbour), Rwanda/Ethiopia (public-investment-led, services and air logistics). Literature leads: Faye et al. 2004; Limao-Venables 2001; Gallup-Sachs-Mellinger 1999; Paudel 2014/2018; UN-OHRLLS; Awaza PoA.
sea_access.open_question: Size of the penalty and whether it is moderated enough by governance and transit infrastructure to allow a 25+ year spell without mineral rents.

institutions.nepal_status: pending (WGI and other indicators to be retrieved); federal transition since 2015 constitution; political instability history
institutions.transfers: Partly. Literature (Rodrik-Subramanian-Trebbi 2004; Johnson-Ostry-Subramanian 2010) suggests broad institutional quality at spell start was often weak among sustained growers, so weak initial institutions are not by themselves disqualifying; what mattered is credibility and continuity of growth-oriented policy (Growth Report). The Acemoglu-Johnson-Robinson colonial-origins identification does not apply to never-colonised Nepal.
institutions.open_question: Whether frequent government turnover is compatible with the policy continuity observed in long spells.

savings_investment.nepal_status: pending (WDI/NRB/NSO series); national saving is substantially augmented by remittance inflows, unlike domestic-saving-driven East Asian cases
savings_investment.transfers: Partly. High investment accompanied essentially all long spells (Young 1995; World Bank 1993) but Nepal's financing mix (remittances, public capital spending execution) differs; remittance-induced real appreciation under the INR peg (Magud-Sosa 2010; IMF WP 2025/122; South Asia panel 2019) may weaken tradables.
savings_investment.open_question: Whether remittance-financed saving translates into productive domestic investment at comparable rates.

export_orientation_and_manufacturing.transfers: Weakly. Manufacturing-led export escalators (Rodrik 2013) are harder for late developers (Rodrik 2016 premature deindustrialisation) and harder still for landlocked producers facing transit costs. Services exports (IT, tourism) and electricity exports are alternative routes with fewer precedents for 25+ year spells.
export_orientation_and_manufacturing.open_question: Existence of any 25+ year spell driven mainly by services or electricity exports.

energy.nepal_status: hydropower resource endowment; seasonal deficits; export access depends on India's cross-border electricity rules (Agent 05)
energy.transfers: Different in kind. East Asian growers were largely energy importers via sea; Nepal's constraint is grid, storage and cross-border market access rather than resource scarcity. Bhutan is the closest analogue (World Bank Bhutan CEM 2024), which also shows limited employment creation from hydropower. Stern 2011 frames energy as binding when scarce.
energy.open_question: Whether hydropower can be a growth driver beyond enclave rents.

demographics.nepal_status: pending (dependency ratio, working-age share); large labour out-migration reduces the domestic working-age dividend while raising remittances
demographics.transfers: Partly. Bloom-Williamson 1998 dividend mechanism requires domestic employment of the working-age bulge; with high emigration the dividend accrues partly abroad.
demographics.open_question: Size and timing of Nepal's remaining demographic window given migration (Agent 09/10 inputs).
